title: Discovering Adaptive Transmission Programs for Collective Innovation
abstract: arXiv:2608.24545v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Human collective intelligence depends on transmission processes: who shares what with whom, how, and when. While these processes emerge from individual cognition, they can also be directed by deliberate top-down protocols. Prior work has studied how transmission shapes collective outcomes primarily through the lens of network structure, varying who shares with whom and when. But networks are state-agnostic: they cannot condition transmission on what agents know or on the state of the collective. Here, we formalize transmission protocols as state-aware programs that route information and resources based on agent and collective states, and we use LLM-guided evolutionary search to design effective protocols in a collective discovery task. Evolved protocols increase collective performance over standard baselines from the literature by up to 37%. translated_title: 发现集体创新中的适应性传播程序
translated_abstract: 人类集体智能依赖于传播过程：谁与谁分享什么、如何分享以及何时分享。虽然这些过程源于个体认知，但它们也可以由自上而下的有意协议引导。先前的研究主要通过网络结构的视角来研究传播如何影响集体结果，即改变谁与谁分享以及何时分享。但网络是状态无关的：它们不能根据智能体已知的信息或集体状态来调节传播。在此，我们将传播协议形式化为状态感知的程序，这些程序基于智能体和集体状态来路由信息和资源，并在集体发现任务中使用LLM引导的进化搜索来设计有效协议。进化出的协议相比文献中的标准基线，将集体性能提升了高达37%。消融实验证实，状态感知驱动了这一优势：去除内容依赖性同时保留其他因素会降低性能，这强调了传播程序对知识状态和集体动态的适应性是关键。
tldr: 本文提出用状态感知传播程序替代静态网络，通过LLM引导进化搜索，在集体创新任务中将性能提升高达37%，并验证状态感知是核心优势。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces state-aware transmission programs replacing static networks, using LLM-guided evolutionary search to boost collective innovation performance by up to 37%, with state-awareness as the key driver.
